name: SASL
summary: Purely functional language designed by David Turner at the University of St Andrews (1972), initially strict and from 1976 lazy; its 1979 implementation by translation to SKI combinators and graph reduction was highly influential, and it led to KRC and Miranda.

level_notes.0: No original implementation source is published online; the combinator-reduction technique is described in Turner (1979).
level_notes.1: Defined by Turner's SASL Language Manual (St Andrews 1976, revised Kent 1979/1983); a 1981 UBC adaptation of the reference manual is online.
